title: Deduplicate 5 shadowed top-level keys in app_he.arb/app_en.arb — one silently kills a zero-task notification branch
rule: Rule 0 gap (no duplicate-key checker for ARB files)
why: JSON's last-key-wins behavior is confirmed against the generated Dart output: lib/l10n/app_localizations_he.dart's todaysLearning(count), errorLoadingTasks(error) and notificationReminderBody(taskCount, curriculumCount) all match the SECOND (later) ARB definition, not the first. No checker anywhere (make audit, arb-parity, flutter analyze) catches a duplicate top-level key within a single ARB file, so 3 of the 5 duplicate pairs carry genuinely different text: an editor who fixes the first (now-dead) copy of todaysLearning or errorLoadingTasks has the fix silently discarded. Worse, notificationReminderBody's line-1765 definition had a deliberately-written zero-task branch (he: 'אין משימות להיום — שמרו על הרצף!' / en: 'No tasks today — stay on track!'); a later duplicate insertion at line 2636/2834 (identical pattern in app_en.arb) replaced it with a two-way plural that has no zero case at all. It is not live-broken today only because the sole caller, lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:517, has an unrelated 'D2 fix' guard (`if (taskCount == 0) { cancel; return; }`) that happens to prevent taskCount=0 from ever reaching the l10n call — if that guard is ever removed or a second caller is added, Intl.pluralLogic falls to `other` and produces 'You have 0 tasks…' instead of the friendly copy that still sits, unused, in the file. The identical 5-key duplicate set exists in app_en.arb too, confirming this is a systemic missing-checker gap, not a one-off typo.
recommendation: Add a Rule-0 checker (tool/ script or a test/l10n/ test) that fails when any top-level key string appears more than once in app_en.arb or app_he.arb, wired into make audit/ci. Then resolve the 5 duplicates: keep todaysLearning's parameterized form (matches its @todaysLearning metadata), keep errorLoadingTasks's live copy or fix the grammar deliberately, and decide whether notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch should be restored (and its caller's guard removed) or the dead ARB text deleted — don't leave orphaned content either way.
acceptance_criteria: A new checker/test fails when a top-level ARB key is duplicated, and is part of make audit or make ci.
app_en.arb and app_he.arb each contain todaysLearning, errorLoadingTasks, today, notificationReminderTitle, and notificationReminderBody exactly once.
notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch is either wired to a real caller or its vestigial ARB text is removed — no orphaned/unused ICU branch remains.
